facts: Draw each subfunction only over the interval where it applies.
An included endpoint takes a filled dot ($\bullet$), and an excluded endpoint takes an open circle ($\circ$).
If two branches meet at the same point and one includes it, the filled dot covers the open circle and the graph joins.
Put arrowheads on ends that continue forever, and dots only where a branch stops.
The domain is every $x$ that is used, and the range is every $y$ that comes out, written in interval notation.
The graph is **even** if it reflects in the $y$-axis ($f(-x) = f(x)$), and **odd** if it has $180^{\circ}$ rotational symmetry about the origin ($f(-x) = -f(x)$).
steps: Identify the subfunctions and their domain intervals
Calculate the boundary values and determine whether each endpoint is open ($\circ$) or filled ($\bullet$)
Plot the subfunctions on their intervals and mark open/closed endpoints

foundation.question_text: Sketch the graph of $f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 2, & x < 0 \\ 2 - x, & x \ge 0 \end{cases}$.
Sketch the graph of $f(x) = \begin{cases} -x - 1, & x \le 1 \\ x - 1, & x > 1 \end{cases}$, marking all endpoints clearly.
Sketch the graph of $f(x) = \begin{cases} 4 - x^{2}, & x \le 0 \\ 4 + x, & x > 0 \end{cases}$.
Sketch the graph of $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x, & x < 1 \\ x^{2} + 1, & x \ge 1 \end{cases}$.
Determine the domain and range of the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 1, & x \le 0 \\ 1 - x^{2}, & x > 0 \end{cases}$.
foundation.solution_text:
The domain is $(-\infty, 0] \cup (0, \infty) = (-\infty, \infty)$.
For $x \le 0$, $y = x + 1$ produces outputs $(-\infty, 1]$.
For $x > 0$, $y = 1 - x^{2}$ produces outputs $(-\infty, 1)$.
The combined set of outputs is $(-\infty, 1]$.
$\text{Domain} = (-\infty, \infty)$
$\text{Range} = (-\infty, 1]$

foundation.question_text: Determine whether the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x, & x < 0 \\ -2x, & x \ge 0 \end{cases}$ is even, odd, or neither.
foundation.solution_text:
Test symmetry using $f(-x)$:
For $x > 0$, $-x < 0$, so $f(-x) = 2(-x) = -2x$.
Since $f(x) = -2x$ for $x \ge 0$, we have $f(-x) = f(x)$ for all $x$.
The graph is symmetric under reflection across the $y$-axis.
The function is even.

foundation.question_text: Sketch the piecewise function $f(x) = \begin{cases} -2, & x < -1 \\ 2x, & -1 \le x \le 1 \\ 2, & x > 1 \end{cases}$.

development.question_text: Sketch the graph of $f(x) = \begin{cases} -x, & x \le 0 \\ x^{2} + 1, & x > 0 \end{cases}$ and state its range.
Find the domain and range of $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3 - x, & x < 2 \\ 2x - 3, & x \ge 2 \end{cases}$ in interval notation.
development.solution_text:
Domain is all real numbers: $(-\infty, \infty)$.
For $x < 2$, $y = 3 - x > 1$, output is $(1, \infty)$.
For $x \ge 2$, $y = 2x - 3 \ge 1$, output is $[1, \infty)$.
The union is $[1, \infty)$.
$\text{Domain} = (-\infty, \infty)$
$\text{Range} = [1, \infty)$

development.question_text: Determine whether $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^{2}, & x < 0 \\ -x^{2}, & x \ge 0 \end{cases}$ is even, odd, or neither.
development.solution_text:
For $x > 0$, $-x < 0$ so $f(-x) = (-x)^{2} = x^{2}$.
Compare with $-f(x)$ for $x > 0$:
$-f(x) = -(-x^{2}) = x^{2}$
Since $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for all $x$, the graph has rotational symmetry of $180^{\circ}$ about the origin.
The function is odd.

development.question_text: Sketch $f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 3, & x < -1 \\ x^{2} + 1, & x \ge -1 \end{cases}$, showing the coordinates of the endpoint at $x = -1$.

The piecewise function $g(x) = \begin{cases} 4, & x < -2 \\ x^{2}, & -2 \le x \le 2 \\ 4, & x > 2 \end{cases}$ is plotted.
State its domain, range, and parity.
development.solution_text:
Domain is $(-\infty, \infty)$.
On $[-2,2]$, $y = x^{2}$ has vertex $(0,0)$ and endpoints $(-2,4)$ and $(2,4)$, giving outputs $[0,4]$.
On $(-\infty,-2)$ and $(2,\infty)$, $y = 4$.
$\text{Range} = [0, 4]$
Since $g(-x) = g(x)$ for all $x$, the function is even.

development.question_text: Test whether $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 1, & x < 0 \\ 2x - 1, & x \ge 0 \end{cases}$ is even, odd, or neither.
development.solution_text:
Evaluate $f(2)$ and $f(-2)$:
$f(2) = 2(2) - 1 = 3$
$f(-2) = 2(-2) + 1 = -3$
Notice $f(-2) = -f(2)$.
Now test general $x > 0$:
$f(-x) = 2(-x) + 1 = -2x + 1$
$-f(x) = -(2x - 1) = -2x + 1$
Since $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for all $x \neq 0$, but $f(0) = -1 \neq 0$, the function fails the odd condition at $x = 0$.
The function is neither even nor odd.

mastery.question_text:
A function is defined by $f(x) = \begin{cases} -(x+2)^{2} + 4, & x < 0 \\ 2 - x, & 0 \le x < 3 \\ 1, & x \ge 3 \end{cases}$.
Determine its range in interval notation.
mastery.solution_text:
Analyze each branch:
For $x < 0$, $y = -(x+2)^{2} + 4$ has vertex at $(-2,4)$ and open endpoint at $(0,0)$, giving output $(-\infty, 4]$.
For $0 \le x < 3$, $y = 2 - x$ gives output $(-1, 2]$.
For $x \ge 3$, $y = 1$.
The union of all outputs is $(-\infty, 4]$.
$\text{Range} = (-\infty, 4]$
